title: AdmBridge: Runbook Interpreter + Safety Adapter for Admin Utilities
creator: Marisol Chen
description:
Goal: Build 'AdmBridge', a lightweight runbook interpreter that converts existing Markdown+snippets runbooks into typed task graphs consumable by the admin utilities surface. It must include a pluggable Safety Adapter that enforces RBAC, dry-run validation, and a sandboxed execution environment for side-effecting steps.

Scope:
- Parser: translate Markdown checklists, code blocks, and special annotations (>>action, >>query, >>confirm) into typed task objects.
- Runtime: provide an executor library for the admin console and CLI that can run tasks with tracing, idempotency checks, and retry policies.
- Safety Adapter: enforce guardrails (RBAC, rate limits, approval gates) and provide a fail-open/closed policy per project.
- Integrations: connectors for GitHub PRs, PagerDuty, Datadog dashboards, and the admin telemetry pipeline.
- Migration: helper to re-encode ~120 legacy runbooks to AdmBridge format and a backward-compatible passthrough for older runbooks during rollout.

Non-goals: full orchestration engine, long-running distributed workflows (we will hand off to task scheduler if orchestration is needed).
acceptance_criteria: Interpreter parses 90% of legacy runbook patterns without manual edits
Safety Adapter blocks any step that performs write operations without a valid token + approval when project policy = strict
End-to-end smoke in staging: run a three-step runbook that checks a service, reboots a worker, and validates service health (with dry-run flagged and then real run)
Telemetry emitted per-step with tags: runbook_id, task_id, actor, mode(dry|live), outcome(success|error|blocked)
Migration tool can bulk-convert 50 runbooks/hour on provided staging cluster
comments: 2025-01-15 - Triage: Created by Marisol. Initial scope sketched after postmortem for INC-2025-004 where an oncall script caused drift due to missing approval gate.

2025-01-20 - Arch meeting: Decided to implement interpreter + lightweight executor locally in the console process to minimize infra surface. Trade-off: tighter coupling vs faster rollout. Action: prototype parser in Go. - Ravi

2025-01-24 - Prototype update: Parser handles checklist->tasks and parses code-block actions. Early edge case: embedded SQL blocks need explicit >>query annotation. Added test fixtures and a corpus of 42 legacy runbooks for fuzzing. - Ravi

2025-01-29 - Security review prep: Security requested sandbox option. Evaluated Lua and WebAssembly. Chosen: wasmtime-based WASM sandbox for deterministic resource budgeting and language-agnostic adapters. Rationale documented in PRD link. - Marisol
2025-02-01 - Integration note: PagerDuty connector will use short-lived tokens from Ops KMS. Need to coordinate with infra for token mint endpoint (ENG-271888). - Ravi

2025-02-03 - QA smoke: Dry-run path exercised in staging; approval gate modal shown, and telemetry emitted. One flake observed where the approval modal blocked for 5+s due to RBAC lookup latency; follow-up: cache approvals per-session (spike ticket created). - QA

2025-02-05 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/admbridge/pull/87 contains parser, executor stubs, and wasm sandbox harness. Requesting review from @sylvia and @james. Pending: test coverage for permission caching, migration tool benchmarks. - Ravi

decisions: Use wasmtime-based WASM sandbox for runbook step execution (deterministic, resource-limited)
Console-embedded executor for fast feedback; heavy orchestrations will be handed to the task-scheduler service
Default migration mode: preview (dry-run) with opt-in live rewrites. Migrate in waves by project/team.
